name: Flow Cytometry Staining
description: Surface and intracellular marker staining protocol for flow cytometry analysis. Includes live/dead discrimination, Fc blocking, surface staining, and optional fixation. Adjust antibody panels and gating strategy to your experiment.
source_note: General educational template for multi-color flow cytometry staining.

steps.title: Prepare single-cell suspension
steps.description: Prepare single-cell suspensions from tissues (mechanical dissociation, enzymatic digestion) or harvest cultured cells. Filter through 40–70 µm cell strainer to remove clumps. Transfer to FACS tubes or wells in a 96-well V-bottom plate.
steps.notes: Keep cells on ice throughout. Work quickly. Keep cell count 1–5×10⁶ per sample.
steps.warnings: If using sodium azide in FACS buffer: toxic — wear gloves; azide also inhibits intracellular signaling.

steps.title: Count and pellet cells
steps.description: Count cells if needed. Centrifuge to pellet. Aspirate/remove supernatant.
steps.notes: Adjust cell count to 1–5×10⁶ cells per staining reaction.

steps.title: Viability staining
steps.description: Stain with a viability dye (e.g., LIVE/DEAD fixable dyes or propidium iodide) to discriminate live from dead cells in the analysis. Apply per manufacturer's instructions in PBS without serum.

reagents.name: Viability dye (e.g., LIVE/DEAD Fixable Aqua or PI)
reagents.notes: Dilute in PBS without serum for fixable dyes

steps.notes: Serum in the buffer will quench fixable viability dyes. Wash once with PBS before adding viability dye.

steps.title: Wash with FACS buffer
steps.description: Add 2–3 mL FACS buffer. Centrifuge and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Fc receptor blocking
steps.description: Block Fc receptors to reduce non-specific antibody binding. Use anti-CD16/32 (mouse) or human TruStain FcX. Incubate on ice.

reagents.name: Fc block (e.g., anti-CD16/32 or TruStain FcX)

steps.notes: Skip Fc blocking step only if no Fc receptor-expressing cells are present. For mouse cells: anti-CD16/32 (clone 93 or 2.4G2). For human cells: human serum or TruStain FcX.

steps.title: Surface antibody staining
steps.description: Add the antibody cocktail (pre-mixed in FACS buffer) directly to cells without washing. Incubate in the dark on ice. Include single-color controls and FMO controls for setting gates.

reagents.name: Surface antibody panel (pre-titrated antibodies in FACS buffer)

steps.notes: Titrate antibodies beforehand to determine optimal concentration. Incubation can be extended to 45 min for difficult antibody-antigen pairs.
steps.warnings: Keep samples protected from light throughout staining.

steps.title: Wash to remove unbound antibody
steps.description: Add 2–3 mL FACS buffer to each sample. Centrifuge and aspirate supernatant. Repeat wash once for cleaner staining.
steps.notes: Two washes recommended to reduce background.

steps.title: Fix cells (optional, for surface-only panel)
steps.description: If fixing cells for later acquisition or biosafety requirements, resuspend in fixation buffer (1–4% paraformaldehyde in PBS, or commercial fixative). Incubate and wash. Fixed cells can be stored at 4°C up to 1 week.

reagents.name: Fixation buffer (e.g., 2% PFA in PBS, or BD Cytofix)

steps.notes: Skip this step for unfixed live-cell analysis. Fixed cells must be analyzed by flow cytometry within 24–72 h.
steps.warnings: Paraformaldehyde is toxic and a potential carcinogen. Handle in fume hood. Dispose per institutional guidelines.

steps.title: Resuspend and acquire on flow cytometer
steps.description: Resuspend cells in an appropriate volume of FACS buffer (300–500 µL per tube). Acquire samples on the flow cytometer. Start with unstained and single-color controls for instrument setup.
equipment: FACS tubes (if using plate, transfer or use plate reader head)
steps.notes: Acquire unstained → single colors → FMO controls → experimental samples. Record instrument settings. Collect ≥10,000 events per sample (more for rare populations).
steps.warnings: If unfixed: acquire as soon as possible. Cell viability decreases over time.
